Basically what is the best way to keep focused. I tend to start a lot of projects but get bored with them very easily and end up quitting. I'm trying to change that.
What is the best way to stay focused on a large project?
break it down into weekly and daily goals. then just complete each little goal and before you know it you will achieve something big

The hardest part of that is when you are also learning stuff as you go and so you might not know much about what goals to make.

I'm in this process at the moment with coding. I know what I need to do, but breaking it down into steps is hard because I am still learning the necessary language to make it happen.
Figure out what it is that distracts you. Decrease your amount of time spent doing those things. Do what another voater suggested and break it down into smaller goals and chunks.

ADDERALL.

And if that's not availible, plan it out. Also, delegate if you can.

Break them down into sub projects.

Goals to be accomplished as part of the whole.

You'll have a better sense of progress, application and accomplishment if you're crushing a handful of individual problems on their own merits, than if you're grinding your way up a long and varied hill.

Have project plan that lists all the tasks to completion.

Each morning, physically write down the tasks you think you can finish that day as a checklist, and mark them off as you finish them. If you are anything like me, you will have that list done by Noon.

Having the list gives you a focus, so use it.

Take breaks if you need. If you get burned out it'll stop being fun and take a longer time because you're hating the process. I have a handful of projects i'm working on right now.
